title: Making low alloy ultrahigh strength steel tough by high-density NiAl clusters
abstract: A novel low alloy ultrahigh strength steel was developed by introducing extremely high-density NiAl clusters (\~ 4.88 × 10<sup>24</sup> m<sup>−</sup> <sup>3</sup>). The steel exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of \~ 1.9 GPa, a total elongation of \~ 15 %, a Unotch impact absorption energy of \~ 80 J and a fracture toughness of 108 MPa⋅m<sup>1/2</sup>. The precipitation behavior and the toughening mechanisms were systematically investigated. Highly dispersed nano-NiAl clusters and submicron ε-carbides precipitate independently, although a small fraction of NiAl clusters interacts with Si during precipitation, thereby increasing the availability of heterogeneous nucleation sites. NiAl clusters promote uniform dislocation distribution, suppressing pile-ups at boundaries and delaying crack initiation. The study revealed multi-scale toughening mechanisms, including large dimple growth, uniform plastic deformation, secondary crack formation, and extensive crack deflection, which collectively result in a \~ 23 % improvement in impact absorption energy. These findings demonstrate that dual-precipitation of NiAl cluster and ε-carbides and dislocation-precipitate interactions provides an effective strategy for achieving high toughness at a tensile strength of \~ 1.9 GPa in low alloy ultrahigh strength steels.
